subject: EU-only processing, SCCs and export-risk mitigation — attestation request
body:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: legal@horizonhealth.com; security@horizonhealth.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only processing, SCCs and export-risk mitigation — attestation request

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward a procurement decision for the patient-triage feature and need to confirm a few things so our infosec/legal teams can sign off:

1) Can Redwood commit to EU-only processing for Horizon tenant data? We need an operational description (routing, hosting regions, failover behavior) and a contractual attestation we can include with our procurement docs.

2) SCCs — do you use the EC standard contractual clauses for controller-processor? Will Redwood sign the SCCs as part of the contract, and do you provide an Annex with sub-processor list and export-risk controls?

3) Schrems II / transfer risk: Horizon is required to run a short transfer-risk assessment and would like to understand Redwood's mitigations (encryption at-rest, encryption-in-transit, key custody options, Russian/US-intelligence access risk commentary, and any contractual limits).

Can you share the attestation and a short M A P (mutual action plan) template we can add to our purchasing docs? We're aiming for a final decision by end of September.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Security Programs
Horizon Health

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com; aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing, SCCs and export-risk mitigation — attestation request

Hi Marta — great to hear from you. Short answer: yes. More detail below and attaching an Annex draft and a short MAP template.

Attached: Redwood_SCCs_AnnexA_v2.pdf (contains sub-processor list, hosting locations, and recommended Annexes), Horizon_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Operational summary:
- EU-only processing: By default Horizon tenant data is pinned to EU regions (Frankfurt, Amsterdam) with a regional control plane. We enforce region-level routing at the edge and have network policies to prevent cross-region routing for customer data labeled for EU-only processing.
- Failover behavior: In the event of an EU-region outage we have two options (customer-selectable):
  a) Automatic failover to a warm EU replica in a secondary EU region (Amsterdam <> Dublin), or
  b) Hold writes and return 503 with a signed SLA exception until EU capacity is restored.
- Data exports: Exports initiated by customer users are routed through the designated EU export gateway. Administrative exports for support are restricted and require explicit written approval; audit logs record every export.

SCCs & contractual attestation:
- Redwood will sign the EC Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor). We provide an Annex A with the current sub-processor list and Annex B describing technical measures. The attached PDF is our draft Annex A (please note this is a working version; we'll produce a finalized Annex at contract execution).
- We can supply a one-page attestation letter for inclusion in your procurement packet that confirms: EU-only processing configuration, sub-processor commitments, and our commitment to sign SCCs.

Schrems II / transfer-risk mitigations:
- Data-in-transit: TLS 1.3 with strict cipher suites.
- Data-at-rest: AES-256 with customer-configurable envelope encryption.
- Key custody: Customer-managed keys via KMS is available on Redwood Dedicated and Private; for Redwood Hosted we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) integration with major cloud KMS providers.
- Access controls: Role-based access, privileged access approvals, and mandatory 2FA for operators.
- Legal & jurisdictional commentary: We recognize buyer concerns re: foreign government access. For Hosted we publish our transparency report and any law-enforcement requests by region. For the highest assurance, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where keys and control plane can be restricted to your VPC and jurisdiction.

Next steps suggested (from MAP):
1) Horizon to confirm preferred failover behavior (automatic EU failover or hold-writes).
2) Redwood to provide the short attestation letter + finalized Annex A by contract signature.
3) Horizon legal to share any required redlines for SCC Annex B.
4) Optional: schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with our infra team to demonstrate routing and KMS flows.

Kimberly and Rishi — tagging you for technical detail/anything missing in the summary. Aditya, can you prepare the 1-page attestation by EOD Monday?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0132

Subject: Re: EU-only processing, SCCs and export-risk mitigation — attestation request

Marta, quick technical clarifications:
- Our region routing enforces tenancy at the service mesh layer; metadata that identifies tenant region is validated at the edge and any misrouted requests are dropped and logged.
- Our KV cache uses per-tenant namespacing; caches are not replicated across regions for EU-only tenants unless you opt in.
- We can produce a short network diagram showing egress controls and edge routing (attaching redwood-eu-hosting-diagram.png).

If Horizon prefers the stricter path, choose "hold-writes" for the procurement doc — that reduces residual export risk because no customer data leaves the primary EU region during failover.

Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: redwood-eu-hosting-diagram.png

Hi all — adding two more mitigation points for Horizon's assessment:

1) Endpoint encryption with per-tenant ephemeral session keys that are rotated hourly for API traffic. This lowers access-time risk from legal process directed at cloud providers.
2) Customer audit package: for procurement we can bundle a redacted SOC 2 + listing of last 12 months of access logs (redacted) and the sub-processor attestations required for SCCs.

If Horizon's legal needs bespoke contractual language around US intelligence access, we can propose a limited liability cap and supplemental covenant around notification and transparency.

-Rishi

Draft attestation (one page):
Redwood Inference — EU-only Processing Attestation
Date: 2027-09-12
We hereby attest that when a customer elects EU-only processing for a tenant, Redwood Inference will:
- Pin processing and storage to the EU regions listed in Annex A (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Dublin).
- Enforce region-level routing and prevent automated cross-region data replication for EU-only labeled tenants.
- Offer customer-managed encryption keys through supported KMS integrations and provide audit evidence of key usage on request.
- Sign the EU Commission's standard contractual clauses (controller-processor) at contract execution and provide a complete Annex listing current sub-processors.

This attestation is intended for procurement review and is subject to the contract execution.

Signature: Laura Bennett, Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks, everyone. This is very helpful and mostly what we needed. A few quick asks before I share with legal:
1) Can you put the attestation on Redwood letterhead and include a contact (phone/email) for a named signatory?
2) For the MAP, we'll accept "hold-writes" as the default; please update the spreadsheet with that option.
3) Legal asked whether Redwood provides a mechanism to log and produce the subset of access requests from foreign governments (date, region, legal basis) — even redacted — for audit. If that's possible, can we add that to the attestation as a commitment to provide reasonable transparency?

If you can get the updated attestation and the finalized Annex A by EOD Monday our procurement team will route to legal.

Best,
Marta
